hexguide.categories.description: This section was written by my hand — of that I am certain — and yet whether it truly comes from my hand is another matter. I remember leaving my mark in this notebook word by word, and still I cannot help but wonder for whom these sections were written. What reader was I hoping for back then? It is a question worth pondering — one that is sometimes even frightening.$(br2)$(o)"All that I know, I speak freely."$()

hexguide.page.casting.hexguide: I use this notebook to record my understanding of Hex Casting, and in my studies it will always accompany me, from the very beginning to the very end.$(br2)I suspect the knowledge in this book may grow too vast and complex for any mind to grasp at once, so I am determined to write down my deeper understanding of the craft here. For those who come after...$(br2)$(o)But who will ever read my $(thing)notes$()? And who will read the $(l:hexcasting:guide)notes on the notes$()?$()
hexguide.page.casting.into: "I shall go and see, I shall go and know, I shall learn what I seek. Though the named shall return to the void, and the knowing shall be bound to the path, human toil yields nothing in the end — yet strive with all one's heart, and die halfway, facing the Great Work, with no regrets in life."
hexguide.page.guide.actions.0: Hex casters manipulate Iotas, and through them the objective world. The tools used to manipulate, multiply, consume, and transform Iotas — and thereby rewrite reality — are what this text calls $(thing)Actions$(). In general, most $(thing)Actions$() correspond to a meaningful $(thing)pattern$(); by drawing those patterns on the grid, we can execute the corresponding action. If an action cannot actually be executed, you will run into a $(thing)mishap$(). This makes it clear: patterns do not always correspond to actions, so there are patterns with no meaning — draw them and you will suffer a mishap.
hexguide.page.guide.actions.1: Likewise, not every action that can be performed has a corresponding pattern, but I will not go into that here. Next come Spells. In the narrow sense, a $(thing)Spell$() refers to the series of patterns in the Spells section of this book that affect the world — for example $(l:hexcasting:patterns/spells/basic#hexcasting:explode)$(action)Explosion/$. Most spells merely consume Iotas, performing no complex manipulation of them, while costing more or less media. In a broader sense, hex casters also call any carefully crafted list of patterns a "spell" or a "hexcast". Understanding and distinguishing these concepts is important for learning and mastering Hex Casting.
hexguide.page.guide.actions.2: The essence of casting should then be obvious: use patterns like $(l:hexcasting:patterns/basics#hexcasting:get_caster)$(action)Mind's Reflection/$ and $(l:hexcasting:patterns/basics#hexcasting:raycast)$(action)Archer's Distillation/$ to draw Iotas from the world, use $(l:hexcasting:patterns/stackmanip)stack manipulation$() patterns such as Jester's Gambit and Gemini Decomposition to arrange the order, quantity, and types of Iotas on the stack to suit the spell, then execute the spell pattern. That is the fundamental method of casting.
hexguide.page.guide.continuation.0: 延续，是人与自然的约定，发自人心而被铭刻于自然的伟岸身躯之上的宏伟蓝图。直白点说，$(thing)延续是将要被执行的那些操作们$()。当我用法杖一个一个的绘制图案时，延续为空，因为自然并不知道我将要绘制什么图案。$(br2)而当我借由$(l:hexcasting:patterns/meta#hexcasting:eval)赫尔墨斯之策略$()这种元运行来执行操作时，我便与自然定下约定：“我将如此操作。”
hexguide.page.guide.continuation.1: 这约定的将要执行的一系列操作的序列，便是延续。像是赫尔墨斯之策略，托特之策略这样的元运行，是向延续中填入新的执行，同时会标记哪一部分延续是由它们填入。$(action)卡戎之策略$()正是凭借这个标记得以从元运行中脱身。$(br2)$(l:hexcasting:patterns/meta#hexcasting:eval/cc)伊里斯之策略$()更为巧妙，它会在像$(action)赫尔墨斯策略$()一样执行图案或图案列表之前先将在它之后将要执行的所有操作封装入一个独特的“跳转”Iota中，那之后再执行它所接受的那个图案或图案列表。
hexguide.page.guide.continuation.2: 如果“跳转”Iota被执行，将立刻终止当前咒术，用其内部所记录的要执行的操作，覆盖掉本来将要执行的操作。举个例子:$(t:iota:aa4924.json)$(hex)此处查看咒术$()$(br2)我们可以把这个咒术按伊里斯之策略的位置拆分成两节，$(t:iota:6b85dd.json)$(hex)此处查看$()和$(t:iota:aa9bc9.json)$(hex)此处查看$(),$(t:iota:aa9bc9.json)$(hex)后者$()被打包进“跳转”Iota，而$(t:iota:6b85dd.json)$(hex)前者$()照常执行，当我们需要退出这次策略的执行时，只需要利用栈操作把这个“跳转”Iota提到栈顶，然后执行之。这样，被保存的操作覆盖了原来要进行的操作，这就是所谓的“跳转”
hexguide.page.guide.escape.0: $(action)Consideration, Introspection, and Retrospection/$ are arguably the three most special patterns of all. Most actions manipulate the stack and the world; these three instead change the "state" of the casting.$(br2)In general, a pattern executes as soon as it is drawn. But if you draw Consideration or Introspection beforehand, subsequently drawn patterns turn yellow, marking them as "escaped". $(l:hexcasting:patterns/patterns_as_iotas)See here for a detailed description of patterns/$.
hexguide.page.guide.escape.1: $(thing)Escaping$() means making an Iota lose its original meaning — instead of executing its corresponding action, it is pushed as a mere Iota into a list or onto the stack.$(br2)In Hex Casting, every Iota has meaning; you might say every Iota corresponds to an "action", except that for most Iotas that action is "throw a mishap". So executing them directly with $(l:hexcasting:patterns/meta)$(action)Hermes' Gambit/$ or Thoth's Gambit throws a mishap.
hexguide.page.guide.escape.2: Thus the secret of Hermes is revealed:$(br2)When Hermes receives a non-list Iota — say, a Pattern Iota — it executes the corresponding "action" directly; when it receives a list, it executes the action of each Iota in turn, as if drawing the patterns one by one on the grid.$(br2)Note that a list Iota's own action is merely to throw a mishap, so a list like iota:list1.json also throws a mishap under Hermes' Gambit.
hexguide.page.guide.escape.3: Escaping has another use: embedding non-pattern Iotas inside patterns. The simplest way is Consideration, written as a list like iota:list2.json. However, Consideration takes priority over Introspection, so it does not work well inside layers of Introspection and Retrospection.$(br2)A more general method of escaping looks like$(br)iota:list3.json$(br)First pack the Iotas into a list with Introspection and Retrospection, then use $(l:hexcasting:patterns/lists#hexcasting:splat)$(action)Flock's Disintegration/$ to unpack the list, pushing its elements onto the stack.
hexguide.page.guide.foreach.0: $(l:hexcasting:patterns/meta#hexcasting:for_each)$(action)Thoth's Gambit/$ looks complex but is actually very simple: it takes two lists — the first is the $(hex)pattern list$(), the second may be called the target list.$(br2)Thoth's Gambit executes the actions in the first list against every element of the second list, with one small twist. For easy understanding: Thoth's Gambit is like working in several stacks identical to the current one,
hexguide.page.guide.foreach.1: pushing one element of the first list into each of them, then executing the actions given by the pattern list in every new stack, and finally gathering the results — all elements of all those stacks — into a single list returned to the original stack.$(br2)For example: suppose the stack holds iota:210983.json; push $(l:hexcasting:patterns/math#hexcasting:add)$(action)Additive Distillation iota:5f5abf.json/$ and then iota:8cac19.json, then use Thoth's Gambit. For every Iota, it creates a new stack identical to the original, pushes the Iota into it, giving$(br)iota:74fc83.json$(br)iota:a5f05d.json$(br)iota:d37a8c.json$(br)then executes iota:5f5abf.json in each of them,
hexguide.page.guide.foreach.2: collecting the results separately, the overall result packed together is:$(br)iota:aa94c6.json$(br2)Thoth's Gambit is mainly used for repeated operations — for example, breaking blocks over a large area, or applying negative effects to all entities in a range. For instance, this spell$(br)iota:1fcc1e.json$(br)first uses $(l:hexcasting:patterns/entities#hexcasting:zone_entity/player)$(action)Zone Distillation: Player/$ to get all entities in range, and $(l:hexcasting:patterns/stackmanip#hexcasting:swap)$(action)Jester's Gambit/$ to arrange them. Then Thoth's Gambit accelerates each of them once. You can try Thoth's Gambit on the $(l:hexcasting:guide/stack#hexguide:spellcasting)grid/$ to the right.
hexguide.page.guide.great.0: 我施展不了这些卓越法术，哪怕我能实实在在的感受到这远古卷轴上记录的图案所展现出的无穷伟力——但一定还有办法，我能感受到在经过卓越法术的洗礼后，我的意识已经发生了$(hex)质变$()，笼罩着整个自然的$(hex)帷幕$()，已经被我掀开了一角，我被准许为自然献上自己的意识，消耗生命来施展法术，那么为了彻底的穿过那个帷幕我需要献上多少呢……
hexguide.page.guide.great.1: 也许，是几乎所有。$(br2)--我已经试过许多方法去讨得自然的欢心，去祈求祂为我降下卓越的$(hex)启迪$()，但那些方法都失败了，我只能铤而走险。$(br2)我将尝试用一次施法将几乎所有的生命奉上，我的全部生命值大约相当于两颗充能紫水晶，一点生命相当于一份紫水晶粉，如果我在完全不携带媒质的情况下，施展消耗19个紫水晶粉的法术……啊，愿我平安归来
hexguide.page.guide.iotas.0: Hex Casting is a craft that uses $(media)media/$ to manipulate Iotas, and through them the world itself, rewriting reality. Iotas are the "names" of all things; we use patterns to obtain Iotas, change their types, compute with them, or execute them — all to draw the information (Iotas) we want from Nature. Then we feed that information to patterns in the right form to achieve the effect we desire. Many patterns combined can create spells as powerful as works of art.
hexguide.page.guide.iotas.1: There are many kinds of Iotas: vectors iota:hexguide:vec0.json, numbers iota:double0.json, entities, patterns, booleans iota:bool0.json, and lists iota:list0.json, among others. Different types carry different meanings: a vector Iota usually represents a position, direction, or velocity; a number Iota is just a number. Most special of all is the Pattern Iota — it stands for a pattern that might itself be cast — and a list of patterns usually means a whole spell made of meaningful patterns. For example iota:list0.json
hexguide.page.guide.iotas.2: Besides those mentioned above, Garbage Iotas like iota:garbage.json and iota:null.json are also common.
hexguide.page.guide.logics.0: Different situations call for different spells — that is obvious. But relying on the caster to switch spells every time is hardly elegant, nor is it convenient. So we can use methods to implement $(thing)"if...then..."$() logic. The most common method uses $(l:hexcasting:patterns/logic#hexcasting:if)$(action)Augur's Exaltation/$: based on the first boolean provided, it keeps either the third or the second element; combined with $(action)Hermes' Gambit/$, this yields an "if...then..." branch.
hexguide.page.guide.logics.1: For example, this spell$(br)iota:5592af.json$(br)first uses Archer's Distillation to get the target coordinates, then $(l:hexcasting:patterns/stackmanip#hexcasting:duplicate)duplicates$() it and checks whether it is null with $(l:hexcasting:patterns/logic#hexcasting:equals)$(action)Equality Distillation/$; if so, it clears the stack with $(l:hexcasting:patterns/stackmanip#hexcasting:pseudo-novice)$(action)Novice's Gambit/$, otherwise it breaks the block. This spell has a more detailed $(l:hexcasting:guide/logics#play)demonstration/$ later on.$(br2)Beyond this method, you can also use $(l:hexcasting:patterns/lists#hexcasting:index)$(action)Selection Distillation/$ to pick different elements of a list by index for multi-way branching — not detailed here.
hexguide.page.guide.meta.0: Meta-execution hides the deepest mysteries of Hex Casting; to understand Hex Casting, you must understand meta-execution. From the notes, we can see that $(l:hexcasting:patterns/meta)$(action)Hermes' Gambit/$ pops a pattern or pattern list from the top of the stack and runs it.$(br2)That is easy to grasp. Yet at the end of these notes, $(l:hexcasting:patterns/meta#hexcasting:halt)$(action)Charon's Gambit/$ is also mentioned — it can stop a cast, but unlike simply lowering the staff or having a mishap interrupt the cast, it can stop those "gambits".
hexguide.page.guide.meta.1: Stop the "gambits"? What does that mean? What is the difference between a pattern executed by meta-execution and one drawn one by one with a staff?$(br2)To explain, we need a basic understanding of the $(hex)mechanics of casting$(). For a single cast, the place that stores the stack, Raven's Thoughts, and other basic data is called the $(hex)Casting Image$(); what stores all the operations the caster is about to perform is called the $(thing)Continuation$().$(br2)When casting by drawing directly with a staff, the caster never told Nature in advance what operations they would perform, so there is no need to consider continuations here.
hexguide.page.guide.meta.2: When we use meta-execution like Hermes' Gambit to run a pattern list, a marker is inserted into the current continuation, and then every operation in the pattern list is inserted after that marker in order. The operations inserted afterwards — those about to be performed — are collectively called the $(thing)Execution Frame$(). The marker and the execution frame together form a $(thing)Casting Boundary$().$(br2)And so the mystery of meta-execution is revealed: Hermes' Gambit creates a casting boundary and pushes an execution frame; if Charon's Gambit is executed inside the frame, it climbs up the continuation, finds the marker Hermes inserted, ends the cast within the boundary,
hexguide.page.guide.meta.3: leaps out of the current meta-execution frame, and continues with any later operations.$(br2)Take iota:d04cdc.json, for example:$(br)Mind's Reflection and Reveal will be executed, while Compass' Purification and Reveal after Charon's Gambit will not.$(br2)Charon works with Thoth's Gambit much the same way: when Charon is met inside Thoth's Gambit, Thoth's traversal stops and execution returns to the level above Thoth.
hexguide.page.guide.mods.hexcassettes.0: $(l:hexcasting:async)磁带$()，可以实现所谓的$(thing)异步咒术$()。通过将咒术$(l:hexcasting:async#hexcassettes:enqueue)入队列$()到磁带，我们便可以在若干时间后在新的$(hex)施法环境$()中释放那个咒术。这里需要注意的是，利用磁带所进行的施法可以认为和将这个咒术进行入队列的施法$(action)没有任何关系$()，磁带延时执行的咒术是在一个完全的新环境中执行的,不继承任何其他环境的栈，渡鸦之思或驱动标记。但是仅仅是让咒术在特定时间后释放并没有什么特别的。
hexguide.page.guide.mods.hexcassettes.1: 如果说，我们可以实现一个这样的咒术：它的效果很简单，$(o)将自身入队列$()。$(br2)这样，它就会在若干时间后再次被释放，这样就形成了所谓的$(thing)守护进程$()——常态式的，持续性的施法。$(br2)实现守护进程有两种方案，一种是将这个法术自身储存在某种$(hex)外部媒介$()中，每次执行时直接去读取外部储存的法术将其延时执行——而那储存的刚好是它自己。
hexguide.page.guide.mods.hexcassettes.2: 另一种方法则是让这个咒术的执行$(action)本身就会再次生成$()一个和$(hex)它本身一样$()的iota，这就颇费功夫了，但是极具美感。让我们先看看这个图案列表$(br)iota:11fa54.json$()这个图案列表执行后会先复制自己，之后再次执行自己，最后死循环报错，这很接近我们想要的，接下来我们看看这个$(br)iota:quine.json$()它执行后变成$(br)iota:real_quine.json**n
hexguide.page.guide.mods.hexcassettes.3: 最终的列表在一次$(hex)赫尔墨斯之策略$()()下仍然得其本身，可以发现，$(t:群体之拆解、1、勘探者之策路、外科医师之提整)iota:q_part.json$()$(br)在最终的列表中出现两次，实际上替代了前文所提的死循环中双子之分解和$(action)赫尔墨斯之策略$()的功能。最终的得到的$(hex)$(t:iota:real_quine.json)这一列表$()本质是两个$(hex)$(t:iota:q_part.json)一样的单元$()互相嵌套，每次执行时都用$(l:hexcasting:patterns/lists#hexcasting:splat)群体之拆解$()解套并用$(l:hexcasting:patterns/lists#hexcasting:replace)外科医师之提整$()替换掉$(hex)$(t:HexPattern[EAST,w])占位符$()。$(br2)顺着这个列表走一遍就很容易理解这个过程了，请看演示
hexguide.page.guide.mods.hexcassettes.4: 那么如何实现持续施法也就显而易见了，以$(t:iota:quine.json)$(hex)这个列表$()为例，如果我们在内层的外科医师之提整后添加数字和入队列以及法术，并且保证前后不额外消耗和增加Iota，那么它就会在一次执行后把包含入队列的咒术入队列，而那个咒术本身又会再次将自己入队列，如此循环，永无休止。最终得到的列表就应当形如：$(br)$(t:要执行的法术放在入队列步骤前后均可)iota:0d164f.json**n$(br2)$(br2)$(o)在被执行后返回本身的咒术，叫做奎因，是通往永恒的钥匙
hexguide.page.guide.mods.moreiotas.0: 我发现了许多实用的新Iota，它们分别是字符串Iota，类型Iota，物品Iota以及矩阵Iota。$(br2)字符串可以储存可以由人直接阅读的信息，相关的$(l:hexcasting:patterns/strings#moreiotas:string/name/set)命名法术$()也可以很方便的去为物品或者实体命名。而$(l:hexcasting:patterns/types)类型Iota$()则带给了我的咒术去区分方块，分辨实体以及检测Iota类别的能力。
hexguide.page.guide.mods.moreiotas.1: 比如说，我们可以预先保存好一个$(hex)$(t:iota:c9412e.json)僵尸类型Iota$()，然后使用$(action)$(l:hexcasting:patterns/types#moreiotas:zone_entity/type)区域之提整：类型$()，来获取到一定范围内的所有僵尸的实体Iota，然后便可以$(hex)轻而易举$()的使用法术来处理这些僵尸。也可以用$(l:hexcasting:guide/logics)占卜师之提整$()来逐个比对$(br2)而要理解物品组Iota，就要先理解什么叫做物品组——手中，箱子里所存放的物品都是以物品组的形式存在的，也就是一个物品类型加上一个数量再加上若干可能会有的特殊数据，它和类型Iota有很好的配合，利用它可以方便的获取容器信息$(l:hexcasting:patterns/items)相关图案在这一章节$()
hexguide.page.guide.mods.moreiotas.2: 至于$(l:hexcasting:patterns/matrices)矩阵$()，比较复杂，为了避免错讹，暂时不记
hexguide.page.guide.spells.arrow.0: 箭，速度越快，伤害越高。如果说能够使用咒术让箭的速度达到极高，便可以用一支箭造成极高的伤害。最容易想到的是用$(hex)连续多次驱动$()的方式，但多次驱动的媒质消耗有些高。$(br2)所以也可以采用$(thing)多次低等级爆炸$()的方法来将箭加速到极快的速度。
hexguide.page.guide.spells.arrow.1: 看这个例子：$(br)iota:arrow.json**n$(br2)$(br2)$(br2)这个法术是先利用非物品和非生物的$(l:hexcasting:patterns/entities#hexcasting:zone_entity/not_item)区域之馏化$()取$(l:hexcasting:patterns/sets#hexcasting:and)交集$()之后获取附近的箭实体，之后在箭矢延施法者视线的反向延长线的一点上引发使用多次0.1级爆炸，这个法术运用$(action)双子之策略$()和$(action)托特之策略$()将低等级爆炸执行了100次，箭被加速到极快，伤害巨大。消耗不到50紫水晶粉。
hexguide.page.guide.spells.arrow.2: 可惜的是哪怕使用$(l:hexcasting:items/hexcasting)施法物品$()，射箭后立刻切换施法也比较麻烦，也许随着我的研究，会有更好的方法吧。
hexguide.page.guide.spells.blocks.0: $(action)$(l:hexcasting:patterns/spells/blockworks#hexcasting:break_block)破坏方块$()也许是最为常用的$(hex)法术$()，但一个一个的破坏未免过于麻烦。$(br2)利用$(l:hexcasting:patterns/meta)托特之策略$()的力量，可以实现大范围的方块破坏。破坏方块接受一个坐标，然后破坏那个坐标上的方块，就算那个位置上空无一物也不会丢出事故。，如果我们要用$(hex)托特之策略$()来破坏大量的方块，
hexguide.page.guide.spells.blocks.1: 那么我们就需要想办法获取我们想要破坏的那些方块的坐标。那么思路便清晰了：$(br)用弓箭手之馏化获取一个方块的坐标，那之后根据这一个坐标获取我们要破坏的所有方块的坐标，怎么获取这些坐标呢？还是用$(hex)托特之策略$()。$(br2)我们看这个例子：$(br)iota:c93f9c.json**n
hexguide.page.guide.spells.blocks.2: 这个列表看似长的吓人，但仔细一看，不过是多次用托特之策略$(hex)重复$()几个类似的图案：$(br)iota:49f422.json$(br)每一次都将原本的一个向量复制成三个，然后其中两个在相反的轴向加上一个单位向量，剩一个不做处理。这样一变成三，三变成九，九变成二十七，就得到了3×3的立方体内的所有方块的坐标。如果最后重复时多执行一个$(action)破坏方块$(),就可以一次性破坏大量方块了。
hexguide.page.guide.spells.boom.0: $(l:hexcasting:patterns/spells/basic#hexcasting:explode)爆炸法术$()是对敌人造成杀伤的好方法。但是让人感到烦恼的是，爆炸会破坏地形。$(br2)好在我们并不是没有办法避免这种事情发生，我们如果用$(l:hexcasting:patterns/stackmanip#hexcasting:duplicate_n)双子之策略$()将目标向量Iota复制成四份，先在那个位置$(l:hexcasting:patterns/spells/blockworks#hexcasting:create_water)构筑一份水源$()，之后释放爆炸——由于在水里发生爆炸便不会破坏方块。
hexguide.page.guide.spells.boom.1: 接着使用$(action)构筑方块$()来填充水源，最后使用$(action)破坏方块$()消除掉所有痕迹，这便是所谓的$(thing)无损爆炸$()。示例：$(br)iota:booms.json**n$(br2)如果利用$(action)区域之馏化$()和$(action)托特之策略$()的话，也许还能把这个法术改造成$(hex)大范围$()的杀伤性法术。
hexguide.page.guide.spells.lights.0: 在使用$(l:hexcasting:patterns/spells/blockworks#hexcasting:place_block)放置方块$()、$(hex)构筑光源$()、$(hex)启迪树苗$()这些法术时，我们会发现利用$(action)弓箭手之馏化$()往往不能获得正确的坐标向量。这是因为弓箭手之馏化会越过空气，树苗这类没有碰撞箱的方块，返回射线追踪所遇到的第一个有实体的方块。$(br2)但是像是构筑光源这样的法术，它所接受的坐标位置上又不能有方块，我们要怎样获取那个方块附近的$(thing)空气的坐标$()呢？
hexguide.page.guide.spells.lights.1: 答案是运用$(l:hexcasting:patterns/basics#hexcasting:raycast/axis)建筑师之馏化$()，这个方块会返回射线追踪遇到的第一个实体方块的那个面的法向量，如果我们将弓箭手与建筑师的结果相加，便可以得到那个方块在视线方向上相邻的空气的坐标。比如说$(br)iota:raycast0.json**n$(br2)对于启迪树苗也是一样的，毕竟在这里空气和树苗并没有什么区分,都是被一般的射线追踪忽略的方块。
hexguide.page.guide.spells.media.0: 施法需要媒质，需要很多很多很多的媒质，我的技术日益精进，而媒质却总是不足……$(br2)媒质，媒质！依靠$(hex)紫水晶洞$()中那些微不足道的产出根本不足以维持施法……我得找到别的办法。$(thing)媒质来自于思维，思维产生于意识，任何的思考都会产生痕量的媒质$()，让我想想，让我想想……也许我可以通过一次施法时少带些紫水晶来节省媒质，也许我可以寻找新的晶洞，但是还不够。
hexguide.page.guide.spells.media.1: 我现在的知识是不足够的，我还需要更多的知识。$(l:hexcasting:patterns/great_spells)卓越法术$()，必须找到卓越法术们，不管是把结晶态的媒质制作成$(l:hexcasting:items/phials)媒质瓶$()，还是$(l:hexcasting:patterns/great_spells/brainsweep)任何其他办法$()，为了媒质，我将不顾一切，也许在沉船或地牢这样的先民遗迹中，会有记载卓越法术的$(thing)远古卷轴$()的踪迹？$(br2)$(o)我不能忍受媒质的缺乏，我不能停下施法……
hexguide.page.guide.stack.0: The place where hex casters manipulate Iotas is the $(l:hexcasting:casting/stack)stack$(). A stack is "last in, first out" — like a pile of plates, stacked one on top of another; you take from the top. The so-called spellcasting grid — simply a canvas — is where patterns are drawn. Drawing the right pattern on the $(l:hexcasting:guide/stack#hexguide:spellcasting)grid$() executes the corresponding action. Right-click with a staff to open the grid; sneak-right-click to open it while clearing both the canvas and the stack. The stack is shown in the top-left corner of the grid.
hexguide.page.guide.stack.1: While casting with a staff you can see the stack directly, so you can draw patterns flexibly to perform the actions you want and release fitting spells.$(br2)But sometimes that is not so convenient, so hex casters prepare a $(action)pattern list$() in advance and write it into a $(l:hexcasting:items/hexcasting)casting item$() or focus, to cast quickly. So what is the difference between casting from an item and casting from a staff? The biggest difference is the $(thing)casting environment$() — it determines the caster, the source of media, the casting hand, and other vital information.
hexguide.page.guide.stack.2: For example, a staff's casting environment is the staff environment, which uses media from your inventory; a $(l:hexcasting:items/ancient_cyphers)cypher's$() environment can only use the media stored within itself.$(br2)In general, each cast creates a new environment carrying new information (the ancients called it a $(thing)Casting Image$()), so each use of a casting item does not inherit the previous stack, Raven's Thoughts, impetus marks, and so on. A staff, however, has a special property: every time you open the grid, it inherits the previous stack and Raven's Thoughts.
hexguide.page.guide.stack.3: Strangely enough, by linking this $(thing)HexBook$() to my mind, it can act much like a staff. Click the Cast button and patterns drawn on the grid will take effect just like a normal staff; click it again to $(l:hexcasting:patterns/patterns_as_iotas)escape$() all patterns drawn afterwards, pushing them onto the stack. The Clr button clears the canvas.
hexguide.page.guide.tips.0: 自然并不总是偏袒咒法师，虽然被授予了施法的伟大权力，但$(hex)错误的操作$()依旧会招来自然的惩罚。这惩罚便是事故。最显而易见的，绘制了错误的图案，没有正确提供操作所需要的Iota，媒质不足，没有转义非图案Iota——这些都会招致事故，不过避免这些小事故只需要仔细看笔记以及不要算错数就行了，并不算什么大事。$(br2)还有一些事故很少遇到，但依然要注意：它们是$(thing)超出栈上限$()和$(thing)超出运行次数$()。
hexguide.page.guide.tips.1: Iota是有$(thing)大小$()的，一般的Iota大小是1，列表则是它其中包含的所有Iota的大小总和再加上1，当栈内的Iota大小超过1023时，便会出现超出栈上限的事故。想要避免它很简单，只需要在每执行完一段咒术之后及时清除栈内所不必要的剩余Iota便好。而所谓$(action)运行次数上限$()，指的是在一次施法中总共可以执行的图案数量的上限，这个值一般是10万，用$(l:hexcasting:patterns/meta#hexcasting:thanatos)塔纳托斯之精思$()可以获取还剩下的运行次数。一般只有一些死循环才会招来这个事故，比如$(br)iota:11fa54.json
hexguide.page.guide.tips.2: 出色的咒法师一般在一次施法之后，不会让自己的栈中留下任何的无用Iota，每一次施法都做的清清爽爽，这样避免事故就很容易了，出了问题也方便维护和修改。$(br2)如果觉得直接管理栈比较麻烦，可以试着使用$(l:hexcasting:patterns/readwrite#hexcasting:local)渡鸦之思$()来临时存放要用到的Iota，或者用$(l:hexcasting:patterns/lists#hexcasting:construct)群体之策略$()把Iota打包成列表之后存进去。
hexguide.page.hexguide_patterns.copy: $(l:hexcasting:guide/hexguide_patterns#hexguide:copy)$(action)Copy Iota/$ copies the top Iota of the stack to your clipboard and prints a clickable reference in chat, so you can share it or paste it into the book. It also saves the Iota as a JSON file under $(thing)hexguide/iotas/$ in the game directory, which can be displayed inline anywhere via a reference like $(br)$(#555555)iota:hash.json/$.
hexguide.page.hexguide_patterns.demo: $(l:hexcasting:guide/hexguide_patterns#hexguide:demo)$(action)Save Demo/$ takes the list Iota on top of the stack (each Pattern Iota in the list becomes one step of the demo), generates a spellplay configuration file, and saves it under $(thing)hexguide/spellplays/$ in the game directory. Drop the generated file into a datapack at $(#555555)data/hexguide/spellplays/$ and it can be played on the Spellcasting Demo page of this book.
hexguide.page.notes.items.0: The $(action)HexBook$() is no ordinary notebook, and no ordinary pen can write in it. Only an Amethyst Pen can engrave my words into paper with media.
hexguide.page.notes.items.1: Paper written with an $(hex)Amethyst Pen$() becomes a Note Scrap containing a Note Iota. Collect Note Iotas into a list and import them into your notes; the following patterns manage those entries.
hexguide.page.notes.items.2: Accepts a list of Note Iotas and imports it as a new note section.
hexguide.page.notes.items.3: Returns a list containing every imported note section, each itself a list of Note Iotas.
hexguide.page.notes.items.4: Accepts an index and returns the corresponding note section as a list of Note Iotas. Indices follow the table-of-contents order.
hexguide.page.notes.items.5: Accepts an index and deletes the corresponding note section.
hexguide.page.notes.items.6: Copies the top Iota to the clipboard and reveals it in chat. If the boolean is true, it also saves the Iota under $(thing)hexguide/iotas/$ so references such as iota:hash.json can render it inline.
hexguide.page.notes_index.0: Here you can write your own notes. Each note is a list of pages; click a note in the list above to browse it. Notes are stored on your server save and can be exchanged with other players as Iotas.
hexguide.page.search.0: Below is a text search box for the contents and entries of The HexBook. Simply type in a name, keyword, or natural language description to find relevant entries. Click any result to jump directly to that page.
